roundReason: Tester's fail at 3ee687b6 (A4/R1): a linked image's link-title line that is an inline HTML tag (, , , ) in a list item, quote or footnote was kept raw; Go reads it as a lazy continuation, the editor's engine as an HTML block, so the past-version view lost the link (fuzz: misreads 10, lost links 15); red test TestRenderWritesALazyHTMLTagTitleLineSoTheEngineReadsItBack (3d0237aa). Architect NARROW with a change of method (dispatch://INFRA-190/comment/fee37e8b-9680-43c6-ba62-cdb6ac670c0f): raw only where Go AND the engine read it back; churn only against main's bytes both hold; generated test and differential run every row through the engine, fuzz corpora added; byte equivalence to 999f2d4b dropped; linear cost with a 100,000-line title test. Fix 5e221be0: rawTitleLinesHold judges each created line syntactically for both readers - a lazy line (container prefix) must read alone as a paragraph or link definitions (readsAloneAsContinuation), the whole-document safety net and rawTitles/escapedTitles removed. Fix 782bc461: makesTable judges every delimiter row under its own header, a delimiter row included, since the engine reads `| - |` over `| - |` as a table (fuzz f513, the one real lost link after 5e221be0). Gates 1a1d08ec and 166cdd6c: differential lists 'rewritten bytes of a document base stores incorrectly' and 'linked image in a write both refuse' ungated. Previous round: Tester's fail at 999f2d4b98c7 (availability): render read the whole document back and re-rendered it once per misread raw title, quadratic (1,000 blank-line titles = 70.8 s on the real server); red test TestRenderIsLinearInImagesWhoseTitlesHoldABlankLine (e39b6dd5). Architect narrowed the round (review_round_cap NARROW, dispatch://INFRA-190/comment/e35d5457-b386-47a2-a6ac-f0f4f513e8ff): only this, linear cost, output byte-identical to 999f2d4b98c7 on the generated test and the differential. Fix 3ee687b69b0e54819f5862a5fb7c8b385a5956fb: each title's created lines are judged as the image is written (rawTitleLinesHold: blank non-last line, leading space/tab/'>', ':::' in a typed block, a typed block behind a prefix, a line opening a block read lazily in containers (continuesParagraph), a table delimiter row under its header (makesTable, header read at most 4 KiB) -> ); render keeps one bounded whole-document check (rawTitleMisread) that re-renders once with every title if a judgement was wrong. Previous round: Tester's fail at 733ebfdb (R3): round 6 wrote an image title's line feed as in list items and block quotes, where the base writes it raw and it reads back as held (lazy continuation), so stored documents churned (differential churn 12, lost fixed points 4); red test TestRenderKeepsAStoredImageTitlesLineFeedInAListItemOrBlockQuote (47d7f3f1). Fix ad3351ac5a56a18175caef51d16d0c5acb1cd7da: a title's line feed is written as the base writes it (raw) wherever that reads back as held in the whole document, judged by reading the rendered document back and comparing every image in order; the image with a raw title at or before the first misread image is written again with , until every image reads back; a heading or table cell never holds one. The generated test now checks the no-churn property (byte-identical to the base wherever the base's bytes read back as held through Parse, ParseForWrite and the engine) beside the inverse property for every row. Gate change e8dbdc4c609229c4a0ccd7b6c43055a8c17e5274: the differential's churn and engine-tree churn gates count only base bytes ParseForWrite also reads back as held; the 2 rows whose raw CR title a write reads as a line feed (decoding-r4:img-title-cr-ref, decoding-r4:img-title-crlf-ref) are listed ungated as 'churn of base bytes a write reads otherwise' - the architect confirmed this definition (Envoy reply 6147063c, 2026-10-26T10:51Z). Previous round: Tester's fail at code head 18e75646 (R2): decodedTitleSuffix wrote a decoded title's line feed raw, so a link title holding a blank line, or any line break in a heading or a table cell, broke its block and the write was refused, a write the base takes; red test TestParseTakesALinkedImageWhoseLinkTitleHoldsALineBreak (0c119da9). The architect also named two image-title shapes the base already refuses (a blank line in an image title, a line break in an image title in a table cell) as the same defect. Fix 733ebfdbd51b2e227203bbd0a71ff6cabc761900: a title's line feed (image title and link title) stays raw only in a top-level paragraph where the image read alone reads back with its titles, so stored titles keep their bytes; in every other block, or when it would not read back, every line feed of both titles is written . The fence is in two places: the upgrade's query (schema_version, editor_schema) and the Hocuspocus token '<schema>:<editor>', whose answer overrides the query's. A bare token is read-only.

A Ctrl/Cmd-click on a linked picture in the editable editor must not be default-prevented by the node view, or ProseMirror never hands it to markdownLinkClickPlugin (picture-view.ts followNoClickWhileEditable); the e2e caught this.

Document dispatch:// clicks are handled in the capture phase (followDispatchLink, both ProofDocument and VersionView), so the past-version view navigates in-app and the link plugin does not also open a new tab.

Round 6: a title's raw line feed is kept only for an image in a top-level paragraph (prefix "", not a heading or cell) whose syntax parsed alone reads back with both titles; a list item or block quote always takes 
, since the raw line feed would not carry the container's prefix. Parse runs only when a title holds a line feed.

Round 7: whether a raw title line feed reads back depends on the whole document (lazy continuation in list items and quotes, a blank line, a line opening a block, typed-block fences), so render reads its own output back with Parse only when some title holding a line feed was written raw, and re-renders with that image's titles as 
; at most one re-render per such image. Node pointers are the asWritten copy's, which the image case sees.

Round 8: a raw title's created lines are lazy continuations in a container (no prefix written), so continuesParagraph reads them inside a quote ('> header\nline'); lineReadsAsText reads lines as prefixed and mis-judged '> b' and '=' lines, so it is not used. A typed block behind a prefix takes no lazy line. The bounded re-render escapes every image, not only the raw ones, so an image escaped by the local judgement cannot turn raw under a changed line.

Round 9: a lazy line's container in the engine is the list item or quote, not the paragraph, so it opens blocks that cannot interrupt a paragraph (HTML type 7, an ordered item not at 1, an empty item); reading the line alone as a document stands in for that reading. The engine also takes a later paragraph line as a table header, so a delimiter row under a delimiter row is a table there though not in Go.
deviations: Pasted HTML title: the image parseDOM uses the img's title attribute when present (the editor's own DOM always carries it) and falls back to alt only when absent, so an editor copy/paste round-trips byte for byte; a foreign README paste gains title "x" as Milkdown's rule gives today.
Reference-style linked images are not in pmdoc's testdata/corpus: pmdoc refuses link reference definitions today (refusals_test.go); the editor test covers them.
The stay-as-today shape ![[![x](i.png)](u)](j.png) is its own diffcorpus document (linked-image-in-alt.md): engine and Go read the outer alt differently at base already, unrelated to links.
A held browser edit that strips a link is reported through a new PendingState.strippedAt notice, not rebuiltAt.
The past-version view now navigates in-app for any dispatch:// link (text, picture, fallback) on a plain click instead of opening a new tab.

Round 3: an image's src is now decoded with the same one-pass decoder as the link (decodeDestination, after micromark): the old unescapeMarkdownText decoded escapes before references and took legacy references without ';', which the editor does not. The differential shows no churn or regression from it.

Round 4: image title and linkTitle now use the same one-pass decoder as src and link (decodedTitleOrNil); text-link href and title keep titleOrNil and titleSuffix unchanged. A title's line feed is written raw as before (no churn for stored titles); a CR, which only a reference puts in a title, is written .
